eligibility.value: The registry publishes no eligibility requirement. Its FAQ answers the question of whether any name can be had with “certain exceptions” and names no qualifying criteria.
eligibility.quote: Yes, right now you have a good chance of getting the name you want with certain exceptions.
eligibility.sourceLabel: about.build FAQ, the registry's own site

intendedUse.value: Plan Bee LLC presents .build as a domain for the building industry, technology companies and makers.
intendedUse.quote: .Build is a top-level domain (TLD) name for the building industry, tech companies, and more.

agreementType.value: Its registry agreement with ICANN, dated 7 November 2013, is recorded as Base, Non-Sponsored — there is no sponsoring community behind the extension.

eligibility.value: No residency requirement at the second level: the registry's allocation rules say an applicant may live in any legal jurisdiction, so a .io name is not tied to the British Indian Ocean Territory.
eligibility.quote: An applicant may reside in any legal jurisdiction.
eligibility.sourceLabel: NIC.IO rules for domain names, clause 3.1

useRestriction.value: The same rules bar sexual or pornographic use and reserve the registry's right to deactivate a name immediately on notice.
useRestriction.quote: No .IO domain may be used, directly or indirectly, for any purpose that is sexual or pornographic or that is against the statutory laws of any Nation.
useRestriction.sourceLabel: NIC.IO rules for domain names, clause 5

thirdLevelRule.value: Third-level names under .io (such as a name under com.io) do require residency in the British Indian Ocean Territory, and one nameserver physically located there.
thirdLevelRule.quote: An applicant must be resident in the British Indian Ocean Territory.
thirdLevelRule.sourceLabel: NIC.IO rules for domain names, clause 4.1

eligibility.value: Anyone may register: Public Interest Registry states that .ORG is open and unrestricted.
eligibility.quote: Yes, .ORG is an open and unrestricted domain. Anyone is allowed to register and use .ORG domain names.

abusePolicy.value: Registration is not unconditional: PIR's anti-abuse policy applies to every TLD it operates, prohibits malware, botnets, phishing and spam, and its only technical remedy is suspending the whole domain rather than a single page.
abusePolicy.quote: This Policy is established for all TLDs for which PIR serves as the Registry Operator (collectively, the “PIR TLDs”).
